sa: केनेषितं पतति प्रेषितं मनः केन प्राणः प्रथमः प्रैति युक्तः ।
केनेषितां वाचमिमां वदन्ति चक्षुः श्रोत्रं क उ देवो युनक्ति ॥
iast: keneṣitaṃ patati preṣitaṃ manaḥ kena prāṇaḥ prathamaḥ praiti yuktaḥ ।
keneṣitāṃ vācamimāṃ vadanti cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ka u devo yunakti ॥

tr.text: Wished by whom is the mind directed to fall (on its objects)? Directed by whom does the foremost vital air move? By whom is wished this speech which the people utter? Who is the radiant being that unites the eye and the ear (with their objects)?

alt.text: By whom missioned falls the mind shot to its mark? By whom yoked moves the first life-breath forward on its paths? By whom impelled is this word that men speak? What god set eye and ear to their workings?

sa: श्रोत्रस्य श्रोत्रं मनसो मनो यद् वाचो ह वाचं स उ प्राणस्य प्राणः ।
चक्षुषश्चक्षुरतिमुच्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल्लोकादमृता भवन्ति ॥
iast: śrotrasya śrotraṃ manaso mano yad vāco ha vācaṃ sa u prāṇasya prāṇaḥ ।
cakṣuṣaścakṣuratimucya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāllokādamṛtā bhavanti ॥

tr.text: Because He is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the speech of speech, the vital air of the vital air, and the eye of the eye, the wise, freeing themselves (from the identity with the senses) and renouncing the world, become immortal.

alt.text: That which is hearing of our hearing, mind of our mind, speech of our speech, that too is life of our life-breath and sight of our sight. The wise are released beyond and they pass from this world and become immortal.

sa: न तत्र चक्षुर्गच्छति न वाग् गच्छति नो मनः ।
न विद्मो न विजानीमो यथैतदनुशिष्यात् ।
अन्यदेव तद्विदितादथो अविदितादधि ।
इति शुश्रुम पूर्वेषां ये नस्तद् व्याचचक्षिरे ॥
iast: na tatra cakṣurgacchati na vāg gacchati no manaḥ ।
na vidmo na vijānīmo yathaitadanuśiṣyāt ।
anyadeva tadviditādatho aviditādadhi ।
iti śuśruma pūrveṣāṃ ye nastad vyācacakṣire ॥

tr.text: The eye does not reach there, nor speech, nor mind, nor do we know (Its mature). Therefore we don’t know how to impart instruction (about It). Distinct indeed is That from the known and distinct from the unknown. Thus have we heard from the ancients who expounded It to us.

alt.text: There sight travels not, nor speech, nor the mind. We know It not nor can distinguish how one should teach of It: for It is other than the known; It is there above the unknown. It is so we have heard from men of old who declared That to our understanding.

sa: यद्वाचानभ्युदितं येन वागभ्युद्यते ।
तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥
iast: yadvācānabhyuditaṃ yena vāgabhyudyate ।
tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥

tr.text: That which is not uttered by speech, that by which the word is expressed, know That alone to be Brahman, and not this (non-Brahman) which is being worshiped.

alt.text: That which is unexpressed by the word, that by which the word is expressed, know That to be the Brahman and not this which men follow after here.

sa: यन्मनसा न मनुते येनाहुर्मनो मतम् ।
तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥
iast: yanmanasā na manute yenāhurmano matam ।
tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥

tr.text: That which one does not think with the mind, that by which, they say, the mind is thought, know That alone to be Brahman, and not this (non-Brahman) which is being worshiped.

alt.text: That which thinks not by the mind, that by which the mind is thought, know That to be the Brahman and not this which men follow after here.

sa: यच्चक्षुषा न पश्यति येन चक्षूंषि पश्यति ।
तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥
iast: yaccakṣuṣā na paśyati yena cakṣūṃṣi paśyati ।
tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥

tr.text: That which man does not see with the eye, that by which man sees the activities of the eye, know That alone to be Brahman, and not this (non-Brahman) which is being worshiped.

alt.text: That which sees not with the eye, that by which one sees the eye's seeings, know That to be the Brahman and not this which men follow after here.

sa: यच्छ्रोत्रेण न शृणोति येन श्रोत्रमिदं श्रुतम् ।
तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥
iast: yacchrotreṇa na śṛṇoti yena śrotramidaṃ śrutam ।
tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥

tr.text: That which man does not hear with the ear, that by which man hears the ear’s hearing, know That alone to be Brahman, and not this (non-Brahman) which is being worshiped.

alt.text: That which hears not with the ear, that by which the ear's hearing is heard, know That to be the Brahman and not this which men follow after here.

sa: यत्प्राणेन न प्राणिति येन प्राणः प्रणीयते ।
तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥
iast: yatprāṇena na prāṇiti yena prāṇaḥ praṇīyate ।
tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥

tr.text: That which man does not smell with the organ of smell, that by which the organ of smell is attracted towards its objects, know That alone to be Brahman, and not this (non-Brahman) which is being worshiped.

alt.text: That which breathes not with the breath, that by which the life-breath is led forward in its paths, know That to be the Brahman and not this which men follow after here.

sa: यदि मन्यसे सुवेदेति दभ्रमेवापि नूनं त्वं वेत्थ ब्रह्मणो रूपम् ।
यदस्य त्वं यदस्य देवेष्वथ नु मीमांस्यमेव ते मन्ये विदितम् ॥
iast: yadi manyase suvedeti dabhramevāpi nūnaṃ tvaṃ vettha brahmaṇo rūpam ।
yadasya tvaṃ yadasya deveṣvatha nu mīmāṃsyameva te manye viditam ॥

tr.text: If you think, ‘I know Brahman rightly’, you have known but little of Brahman’s (true) nature. What you know of His form and what form you know among the gods (too is but little). Therefore Brahman is still to be inquired into by you. I think Brahman is known to me.

alt.text: If thou thinkest that thou knowest It well, little indeed dost thou know the form of the Brahman. That of It which is thou, that of It which is in the gods, this thou hast to think out. I think It known.

sa: नाहं मन्ये सुवेदेति नो न वेदेति वेद च ।
यो नस्तद्वेद तद्वेद नो न वेदेति वेद च ॥
iast: nāhaṃ manye suvedeti no na vedeti veda ca ।
yo nastadveda tadveda no na vedeti veda ca ॥

tr.text: I think not I know Brahman rightly, nor do I think It is unknown. I know (and I do not know also). He among us who knows that knows It (Brahman); not that It is not known nor that It is known.

alt.text: I think not that I know It well and yet I know that It is not unknown to me. He of us who knows It, knows That; he knows that It is not unknown to him.

sa: यस्यामतं तस्य मतं मतं यस्य न वेद सः ।
अविज्ञातं विजानतां विज्ञातमविजानताम् ॥
iast: yasyāmataṃ tasya mataṃ mataṃ yasya na veda saḥ ।
avijñātaṃ vijānatāṃ vijñātamavijānatām ॥

tr.text: It is known to him to whom It is unknown; he to whom It is known does not know It. It is unknown to those who know, and known to those who know not.

alt.text: He by whom It is not thought out, has the thought of It; he by whom It is thought out, knows It not. It is unknown to the discernment of those who discern of It, by those who seek not to discern of It, It is discerned.

sa: प्रतिबोधविदितं मतममृतत्वं हि विन्दते ।
आत्मना विन्दते वीर्यं विद्यया विन्दतेऽमृतम् ॥
iast: pratibodhaviditaṃ matamamṛtatvaṃ hi vindate ।
ātmanā vindate vīryaṃ vidyayā vindate’mṛtam ॥

tr.text: When Brahman is known as the inner Self (of cognition) in every state of consciousness, It is known in reality, because one thus attains immortality. Through one’s own Self is attained strength and through knowledge is attained immortality.

alt.text: When It is known by perception that reflects It, then one has the thought of It, for one finds immortality; by the self one finds the force to attain and by the knowledge one finds immortality.

sa: इह चेदवेदीदथ सत्यमस्ति न चेदिहावेदीन्महती विनष्टिः ।
भूतेषु भूतेषु विचित्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल्लोकादमृता भवन्ति ॥
iast: iha cedavedīdatha satyamasti na cedihāvedīnmahatī vinaṣṭiḥ ।
bhūteṣu bhūteṣu vicitya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāllokādamṛtā bhavanti ॥

tr.text: Here if one has realized, then there is accomplishment. Here if one has not realized, then there is utter ruin. Having realized Brahman in all beings, and having withdrawn from this world, the wise become immortal.

alt.text: If here one comes to that knowledge, then one truly is; if here one comes not to the knowledge, then great is the perdition. The wise distinguish That in all kinds of becomings and they pass forward from this world and become immortal.

sa: ब्रह्म ह देवेभ्यो विजिग्ये तस्य ह ब्रह्मणो विजये देवा अमहीयन्त ।
त ऐक्षन्तास्माकमेवायं विजयोऽस्माकमेवायं महिमेति ॥
iast: brahma ha devebhyo vijigye tasya ha brahmaṇo vijaye devā amahīyanta ।
ta aikṣantāsmākamevāyaṃ vijayo’smākamevāyaṃ mahimeti ॥

tr.text: It is well-known that Brahman indeed achieved victory for the gods. But in that victory which was Brahman’s the gods reveled in joy.

alt.text: The Eternal conquered for the gods and in the victory of the Eternal the gods grew to greatness. They saw, “Ours the victory, ours the greatness.”

sa: तद्धैषां विजज्ञौ तेभ्यो ह प्रादुर्बभूव तन्न व्यजानत किमिदं यक्षमिति ॥
iast: taddhaiṣāṃ vijajñau tebhyo ha prādurbabhūva tanna vyajānata kimidaṃ yakṣamiti ॥

tr.text: They thought, “Ours alone is this victory, ours alone is this glory”. Brahman knew this their pride and appeared before them, but they knew not who this Yaksha (worshipful Being) was.

alt.text: The Eternal knew their thought and appeared before them; and they knew not what was this mighty Daemon.

sa: तेऽग्निमब्रुवन्जातवेद एतद्विजानीहि किमेतद्यक्षमिति तथेति ॥
iast: te’gnimabruvanjātaveda etadvijānīhi kimetadyakṣamiti tatheti ॥

tr.text: They said to Agni: “O Jataveda, know thou this as to who this Yaksha is”. (He said:) “So be it.”

alt.text: They said to Agni, 'O thou that knowest all things born, learn of this thing, what may be this mighty Daemon,' and he said, 'So be it.'

sa: तदभ्यद्रवत् तमभ्यवदत् कोऽसीत्यग्निर्वा अहमस्मीत्यब्रवीज्जातवेदा वा अहमस्मीति ॥
iast: tadabhyadravat tamabhyavadat ko’sītyagnirvā ahamasmītyabravījjātavedā vā ahamasmīti ॥

tr.text: Agni approached It. It asked him, “Who art thou?” He replied, “I am Agni or I am Jataveda”.

alt.text: He rushed towards the Eternal and It said to him, “Who art thou?” “I am Agni,” he said, “I am he that knows all things born.”

sa: तस्मिंस्त्वयि किं वीर्यमित्यपीदं सर्वं दहेयं यदिदं पृथिव्यामिति ॥
iast: tasmiṃstvayi kiṃ vīryamityapīdaṃ sarvaṃ daheyaṃ yadidaṃ pṛthivyāmiti ॥

tr.text: (It said:) “What is the power in thee, such as thou art?” (Agni said:) “I can burn all this that is upon the earth.”

alt.text: Since such thou art, what is the force in thee? Even all this I could burn, all that is upon the earth.

sa: तस्मै तृणं निदधावेतद्दहेति तदुपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन्न शशाक दग्धुं
स तत एव निववृते नैतदशकं विज्ञातुं यदेतद्यक्षमिति ॥
iast: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāvetaddaheti tadupapreyāya sarvajavena tanna śaśāka dagdhuṃ
sa tata eva nivavṛte naitadaśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yadetadyakṣamiti ॥

tr.text: For him (It) placed there a blade of grass and said: “Burn this”. (Agni) went near it in all haste, but he could not burn it. He returned from there (and said:) “I am unable to understand who that Yaksha is”.

alt.text: The Eternal set before him a blade of grass; “This burn;” and he made towards it with all his speed, but could not burn it. There he ceased, and turned back; “I could not know of It, what might be this mighty Daemon.”

sa: अथ वायुमब्रुवन् वायवेतद्विजानीहि किमेतद्यक्षमिति तथेति ॥
iast: atha vāyumabruvan vāyavetadvijānīhi kimetadyakṣamiti tatheti ॥

tr.text: Then (the gods) said to Vayu: “O Vayu, know thou this as to who this Yaksha is”. (He said:) “So be it”.

alt.text: Then they said to Vayu, 'O Vayu, this discern, what is this mighty Daemon.' He said, 'So be it.'

sa: तदभ्यद्रवत् तमभ्यवदत् कोऽसीति वायुर्वा अहमस्मीत्यब्रवीन्मातरिश्वा वा अहमस्मीति ॥
iast: tadabhyadravat tamabhyavadat ko’sīti vāyurvā ahamasmītyabravīnmātariśvā vā ahamasmīti ॥

tr.text: Vayu approached It. It said to him, “Who art thou?” He replied, “I am Vayu or I am Matarsiva”.

alt.text: He rushed upon That; It said to him, 'Who art thou?' 'I am Vayu,' he said, 'and I am he that expands in the Mother of things.'

sa: तस्मिंस्त्वयि किं वीर्यमित्यपीदं सर्वमाददीय यदिदं पृथिव्यामिति ॥
iast: tasmiṃstvayi kiṃ vīryamityapīdaṃ sarvamādadīya yadidaṃ pṛthivyāmiti ॥

tr.text: (It said:) “What is the power in thee, such as thou art?” (Vayu said:) “I can take hold of all this that is upon the earth”.

alt.text: Since such thou art, what is the force in thee? Even all this I can take for myself, all this that is upon the earth.

sa: तस्मै तृणं निदधावेतदादत्स्वेति तदुपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन्न शशाकादातुं
स तत एव निववृते नैतदशकं विज्ञातुं यदेतद्यक्षमिति ॥
iast: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāvetadādatsveti tadupapreyāya sarvajavena tanna śaśākādātuṃ
sa tata eva nivavṛte naitadaśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yadetadyakṣamiti ॥

tr.text: For him (It) placed there a blade of grass and said: “Take this up”. (Vayu) went near it in all haste, but he could not take it up. He returned from there (and said:) “I am unable to understand who that Yaksha is”.

alt.text: That set before him a blade of grass, 'This take.' He went towards it with all his speed and he could not take it. Even there he ceased, even thence he returned: 'I could not discern of That, what is this mighty Daemon.'

sa: अथेन्द्रमब्रुवन् मघवन्नेतद्विजानीहि किमेतद्यक्षमिति तथेति तदभ्यद्रवत् तस्मात्तिरोदधे ॥
iast: athendramabruvan maghavannetadvijānīhi kimetadyakṣamiti tatheti tadabhyadravat tasmāttirodadhe ॥

tr.text: Then (the gods) said to Indra: “O Maghava, know thou this as to who this Yaksha is”. (He said:) “So be it”. He approached It, but It disappeared from him.

alt.text: Then they said to Indra, 'Master of plenitudes, get thou the knowledge, what is this mighty Daemon.' He said, 'So be it.' He rushed upon That. That vanished from before him.

sa: स तस्मिन्नेवाकाशे स्त्रियमाजगाम बहुशोभमानामुमां हैमवतीं तां होवाच किमेतद्यक्षमिति ॥
iast: sa tasminnevākāśe striyamājagāma bahuśobhamānāmumāṃ haimavatīṃ tāṃ hovāca kimetadyakṣamiti ॥

tr.text: In that space itself (where the Yaksha had disappeared) Indra approached an exceedingly charming woman. To that Uma decked in gold (or to the daughter of the Himalayas), he said: “Who is this Yaksha?”

alt.text: He in the same ether came upon the Woman, even upon Her who shines out in many forms, Uma daughter of the snowy summits. To her he said, 'What was this mighty Daemon?'

sa: सा ब्रह्मेति होवाच ब्रह्मणो वा एतद्विजये महीयध्वमिति ततो हैव विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति ॥
iast: sā brahmeti hovāca brahmaṇo vā etadvijaye mahīyadhvamiti tato haiva vidāṃcakāra brahmeti ॥

tr.text: She said: “It was Brahman. In the victory that was Brahman’s you were reveling in joy”. Then alone did Indra know for certain that It was Brahman.

alt.text: She said to him, 'It is the Eternal. Of the Eternal is this victory in which ye shall grow to greatness.' Then alone he came to know that this was the Brahman.

sa: तस्माद्वा एते देवा अतितरामिवान्यान् देवान् यदग्निर्वायुरिन्द्रस्ते ह्येनन्नेदिष्ठं पस्पर्शुस्ते ह्येनत्प्रथमो विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति ॥
iast: tasmādvā ete devā atitarāmivānyān devān yadagnirvāyurindraste hyenannediṣṭhaṃ pasparśuste hyenatprathamo vidāṃcakāra brahmeti ॥

tr.text: Therefore, these gods viz. Agni, Vayu and Indra excelled other gods, for they touched Brahman who stood very close and indeed knew first that It was Brahman.

alt.text: Therefore are these gods as it were beyond all the other gods, even Agni and Vayu and Indra, because they came nearest to the touch of That....

sa: तस्माद्वा इन्द्रोऽतितरामिवान्यान्देवान् स ह्येनन्नेदिष्ठं पस्पर्श स ह्येनत् प्रथमो विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति ॥
iast: tasmādvā indro’titarāmivānyāndevān sa hyenannediṣṭhaṃ pasparśa sa hyenat prathamo vidāṃcakāra brahmeti ॥

tr.text: Therefore is Indra more excellent than the other gods, for he touched Brahman who stood very close and indeed knew first that It was Brahman.

alt.text: Therefore is Indra as it were beyond all the other gods because he came nearest to the touch of That, because he first knew that it was the Brahman.

sa: तस्यैष आदेशो यदेतद्विद्युतो व्यद्युतदा३ इतीन्न्यमीमिषदा३ इत्यधिदैवतम् ॥
iast: tasyaiṣa ādeśo yadetadvidyuto vyadyutadā3 itīnnyamīmiṣadā3 ityadhidaivatam ॥

tr.text: Its instruction (regarding meditation) is this. It is similar to that which is like a flash of lightning or like the winkling of the eye. This is (the analogy of Brahman) in the divine aspect.

alt.text: Now this is the indication of That,—as is this flash of the lightning upon us or as is this falling of the eyelid, so in that which is of the gods.

sa: अथाध्यात्मं यदेतद्गच्छतीव च मनोऽनेन चैतदुपस्मरत्यभीक्ष्णं संकल्पः ॥
iast: athādhyātmaṃ yadetadgacchatīva ca mano’nena caitadupasmaratyabhīkṣṇaṃ saṃkalpaḥ ॥

tr.text: Then (follows) the instruction through analogy on the aspect of the individual self. (It is wellknown that) the mind seems to attain to It, that It is continually remembered by the mind, and that the mind possesses the thought (regarding It).

alt.text: Then in that which is of the Self,—as the motion of this mind seems to attain to That and by it afterwards the will in the thought continually remembers It.

sa: तद्ध तद्वनं नाम तद्वनमित्युपासितव्यं स य एतदेवं वेदाभि हैनं सर्वाणि भूतानि संवाञ्छन्ति ॥
iast: taddha tadvanaṃ nāma tadvanamityupāsitavyaṃ sa ya etadevaṃ vedābhi hainaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni saṃvāñchanti ॥

tr.text: That Brahman is known indeed as Tadvana (worshipful or adorable to all beings); That is to be worshiped as Tadvana. To him who knows It thus verily all beings pray.

alt.text: The name of That is 'That Delight'; as That Delight one should follow after It. He who so knows That, towards him verily all existences yearn.

sa: उपनिषदं भो ब्रूहीत्युक्ता त उपनिषद् ब्राह्मीं वाव त उपनिषदमब्रूमेति ॥
iast: upaniṣadaṃ bho brūhītyuktā ta upaniṣad brāhmīṃ vāva ta upaniṣadamabrūmeti ॥

tr.text: (Disciple:) “Revered sir, speak Upanishad to me.” (Teacher:) “I have spoken Upanishad to thee. Of Brahman verily is the Upanishad that I have spoken.”

alt.text: Thou hast said 'Speak to me Upanishad'; spoken to thee is Upanishad. Of the Eternal verily is the Upanishad that we have spoken.

sa: तस्यै तपो दमः कर्मेति प्रतिष्ठा वेदाः सर्वाङ्गानि सत्यमायतनम् ॥
iast: tasyai tapo damaḥ karmeti pratiṣṭhā vedāḥ sarvāṅgāni satyamāyatanam ॥

tr.text: Of this knowledge austerity, self-restraint and action are the feet, the Vedas are all limbs and truth is the abode.

alt.text: Of this knowledge austerity and self-conquest and works are the foundation, the Vedas are all its limbs, truth is its dwelling place.

sa: यो वा एतामेवं वेदापहत्य पाप्मानमनन्ते स्वर्गे लोके ज्येये प्रतितिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति ॥
iast: yo vā etāmevaṃ vedāpahatya pāpmānamanante svarge loke jyeye pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati ॥

tr.text: He who knows this thus, with his sins destroyed, becomes firmly seated in the infinite, blissful and supreme Brahman. He becomes firmly seated (in Brahman).

alt.text: He who knows this knowledge, smites evil away from him and in that vaster world and infinite heaven finds his foundation, yea, he finds his foundation.
